sec: Scintigraphy Grid, Ophthalmopathy Progression & Eponymous Signs

items.q: Match the scintigraphy finding to the diagnosis on page 912 — 1) Diffuse symmetrical uptake (75-80%), reduced salivary uptake 2) Low or absent uptake, prominent salivary uptake 3) Increased uptake in nodule with contralateral reduced uptake … A) Graves' disease B) Thyroiditis C) Toxic adenoma
items.exp: Scintigraphy table: Graves shows diffuse 75-80% uptake with reduced salivary uptake; Thyroiditis shows low/absent uptake with prominent salivary uptake; Toxic adenoma shows increased uptake in nodule with contralateral reduced uptake. (Book p912)

items.q: On radionuclide scintigraphy, compare physiological uptake against the diffuse uptake seen in Graves' disease:
items.exp: Scintigraphy table: Normal uptake is 25%; in Graves' disease, diffuse uptake reaches 75 - 80%. (Book p912)

items.q: On histopathology of Graves' disease, follicular epithelial cells appear tall columnar with resorbed colloid producing a characteristic ___ appearance.
items.exp: The histological caption on page 912 states: 'Tall Columnar cell resorbed colloid (Scalloped appearance)'. (Book p912)

items.q: What percentage of the hyperthyroid population presents with ophthalmopathy?
items.exp: Under Graves Ophthalmopathy: '30% Hyperthyroid population can present ophthalmopathy'. (Book p912)

items.q: According to the '40/40/20 rule' of Graves' ophthalmopathy, match the presentation category to its percentage — 1) Graves symptoms elsewhere, followed later by ophthalmopathy 2) Graves with ophthalmopathy present at diagnosis 3) Ophthalmopathy as initial presentation (unilateral to bilateral) … A) 40% B) 40% C) 20%
items.exp: The 40/40/20 rule: 40% develop ophthalmopathy later; 40% have ophthalmopathy at presentation; 20% have ophthalmopathy as initial presentation (U/L -> B/L). (Book p912)

items.q: According to the mnemonic 'IM SLOW' for extraocular muscle involvement in Graves' ophthalmopathy, the first muscle affected is the ___ rectus, followed next by the ___ rectus.
items.exp: Under mnemonic IM SLOW: 'First muscle affected : Inferior rectus -> next: medial rectus -> next: Superior rectus -> next: Obliques'. (Book p912)

items.q: What is the full muscle involvement sequence in the 'IM SLOW' mnemonic for Graves' orbitopathy?
opts: Inferior rectus → Medial rectus → Superior rectus → Obliques
Internal rectus → Middle rectus → Superior rectus → Lateral rectus
Inferior oblique → Medial rectus → Superior oblique → Lateral rectus
Inferior rectus → Superior rectus → Medial rectus → Lateral rectus
items.exp: The mnemonic IM SLOW expands to: Inferior rectus -> Medial rectus -> Superior rectus -> Obliques. (Book p912)

items.q: Regarding active Graves' ophthalmopathy: I Radioactive iodine treatment is contraindicated. II Medical management includes smoking cessation and high-dose intravenous steroids.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Page 912 states: 'Radioactive treatment C/I' and 'Rx : stop smoking, High dose IV steroid'. (Book p912)

items.q: Match the eponymous Graves' eye signs — 1) Von Graefe's 2) Joffroy's 3) Stellwag's 4) Dalrymple's … A) Lid lag in down gaze B) Absent creases in the forehead on superior gaze C) Incomplete and infrequent blinking D) Widened palpebral fissure during fixation
items.exp: Eye signs: Von Graefe's = Lid lag in down gaze; Joffroy = Absent creases in forehead on superior gaze; Stellwag = Incomplete and infrequent blinking; Dalrymple's = Widened palpebral fissure during fixation. (Book p912)

items.q: The eponymous sign defined by impairment of ocular convergence in Graves' disease is ___ sign.

A 28-year-old female presents with biochemical thyrotoxicosis (suppressed TSH, elevated free T3 and T4). On careful neck examination, the thyroid gland is completely non-palpable. What does this suggest per page 912?
items.exp: Page 912 contains the note: 'Note : Non palpable gland with thyrotoxicosis = Exogenous cause / thyroiditis'. (Book p912)

items.q: In the Graves' disease management flowchart on page 912, what T3/T4 ratio is characteristic alongside suppressed TSH and elevated free hormones before confirming TRAb positivity?
items.exp: Under management: 'On Investigations : TSH ↓, free T3 ↑, free T4 ↑, T3/T4 > 20 -> Next: Antibody : TSH-(R) Ab +ve -> Next: Diagnosis : Graves disease'. (Book p912)
